title: "Your PDF Could Not Be Processed": Fix Password-Protected or Damaged Book Files | SparkPrep
h1: How to fix "your file could not be processed"
description: KDP or IngramSpark can't open your book PDF. The usual causes are a password, a damaged export or an odd PDF setting. Here's how to fix it.
platforms: Amazon KDP · IngramSpark · Barnes & Noble Press · Lulu
lead: Before a printer can check your book, it has to open it. If it can't, you get a vague "could not be processed" message.
error: Your file could not be processed. Please upload a valid PDF.
errorNote: Paraphrased. Each printer words this a little differently.
why:
Printers' systems need to open every page. The common reasons they can't:

  • A password or security setting, even one that only blocks printing or editing.
  • A damaged file from an export that stopped early, a bad download, or a file synced while still saving.
  • A "PDF" that isn't really one, like a renamed Word or image file, or a web "Print to PDF" with odd settings.
manual: Open the PDF on your computer. If it asks for a password or shows a lock, remove the security: Acrobat → File → Properties → Security → "No Security".
If it won't open cleanly, go back to your original Word, InDesign or Canva file.
Export a fresh PDF straight from that original (File → Save As / Export → PDF), not from a browser or a converter website.
Open the new PDF and scroll through every page to check it's complete.
Re-upload it to your printer and wait for the file review again. If it fails, you start over.

cta.text: SparkPrep tells you straight away if a file can't be read, and every file it exports is a fresh, clean print PDF with no locks.

faq.q: Can I upload a password-protected PDF to KDP?
faq.a: No. Remove any password or security settings before uploading.

faq.q: Why does my PDF open on my computer but fail on KDP?
faq.a: Security settings, a partly damaged export, or unusual PDF features can all pass on your screen but fail the printer's check. A fresh export from the original file usually fixes it.
